patterns_data.top_pattern: Authorization code assignment is distorting the spend signal in CA / VA / PA
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: Authorization coding on paid inpatient and facility claims in CA / VA / PA
key_driver_codes: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC
Other Disorders of Nervous System with MCC
patterns_data.pattern_details: A large share of the apparent increase is tied to how authorization codes are landing on claims rather than a clean change in utilization or reimbursement. CA is the largest issue, with the same pattern also present in VA and PA. This needs to be corrected before using the results for provider action, UM policy changes, or reimbursement decisions.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: If the authorization code logic is wrong, downstream provider, utilization, and clinical actions will be aimed at the wrong drivers.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Reconcile AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION logic across authorization, UM, and claims feeds in CA / VA / PA, reclassify the impacted claims, and rerun attribution before taking provider or policy action.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The flagged issue is an authorization coding or mapping shift and the source groups explicitly require validation before action.
evidence_summary: CA accounts for about +$2.0M of the issue, led by Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC (+$0.5M) and Other Disorders of Nervous System with MCC (+$0.5M).
VA adds about +$0.6M and PA adds about +$0.3M under the same authorization code movement.
Ungroupable and clinically mixed admissions are included, increasing the likelihood that classification is distorting the signal.

patterns_data.top_pattern: Authorized post-acute spend is rising across SNF, NF, and rehab settings
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: PPO Local post-acute care in SNF - FREE STANDING, NF, and Physical Rehab
key_driver_codes: Other Disorders of Nervous System with MCC
patterns_data.pattern_details: Post-acute spend growth is concentrated in free-standing SNF, nursing facility, and rehab settings rather than only in acute hospitals. The increase is being driven by a mix of more admissions and higher paid per admit, with the sharpest spikes in CA SNF/NF activity, VA SNF volume, and small but expensive Physical Rehab cases in CA / WI. This is a site-of-care management issue with network and UM levers, not just a single-provider hospital problem.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Post-acute settings can sustain recurring spend growth if level-of-care decisions, length of stay, and reimbursement are not tightened quickly.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Run a joint post-acute action plan for SNF, NF, and Physical Rehab authorized cases: validate level of care, review length of stay, and renegotiate or steer away from outlier providers where paid per admit is elevated.
evidence_summary: CA SNF - FREE STANDING added about +$0.6M, including 18 more admissions in ungroupable stays with paid per admit up about $1.1K.
VA SNF - FREE STANDING added about +$0.3M with 27 more admissions and paid per admit up about $1.9K.
Physical Rehab in CA / WI added about +$0.5M, including small clusters with paid per admit up roughly $9.1K to $59.8K.
CA NF added about +$0.4M across UTI, cellulitis, and neurologic cases.

patterns_data.top_pattern: CA acute hospital spend is concentrating at Adventist and targeted IP Med/Surg cases
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: CA PPO Local Acute Hospital and IP Med/Surg admissions
key_driver_codes: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC
Other Disorders of Nervous System with MCC
patterns_data.pattern_details: CA acute hospital spend is being pushed by a concentrated mix of more admissions and higher severity in a small set of IP Med/Surg conditions. Adventist Health Simi Valley is the clearest provider concentration point, while UTI, cellulitis, neurologic, and toxic encephalopathy cases are driving much of the clinical lift. This is a focused provider-and-case-mix issue rather than broad statewide inpatient inflation.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: A concentrated acute hospital pattern creates a clear opportunity for targeted UM intervention and provider-specific contract review.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Launch a joint UM and network review of CA authorized acute admissions centered on Adventist, with focus on UTI, cellulitis, and neurologic admissions and comparison to peer hospitals on admission criteria and reimbursement.
evidence_summary: Adventist Health Simi Valley added about +$0.2M in authorized CA acute hospital spend with 12 more admissions.
UTI without MCC drove about +$0.2M clinically with roughly 30 more IP Med/Surg admissions and another +$0.1M operationally in acute hospital claims.
Critical illness myopathy and other toxic encephalopathy added about +$0.3M combined in concentrated neurologic cases.
CA acute hospital utilization also rose in Other Disorders of Nervous System with MCC and Cellulitis with MCC.

key_driver_codes: UNIVERSITY OF KENTUCKY ALBERT B. CHANDLER HOSPITAL
Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC
patterns_data.pattern_details: Outside CA and VA, acute hospital pressure is concentrated in a small set of providers and expensive admission clusters rather than spread evenly across the network. PA and KY are the most actionable points, with additional small but high-cost spikes in CT / GA / OH. The business issue is provider economics on authorized inpatient cases, especially where paid per admit has moved materially higher.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Provider concentration means targeted contract, case-rate, and payment integrity action can address a meaningful share of the increase.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Run provider-specific contract and payment review for Lehigh Valley Hospital - Cedar Crest, University of Kentucky Albert B. Chandler Hospital, and the identified CT / GA / OH acute hospital clusters, prioritizing services with higher paid per admit.
evidence_summary: Lehigh Valley Hospital - Cedar Crest drove about +$0.4M in PA with 12 more admissions and paid per admit up about $9.9K.
University of Kentucky Albert B. Chandler Hospital added about +$0.2M in KY with 8 more admissions and paid per admit up about $8.4K.
GA acute hospital UTI admissions added about +$0.2M on 24 more admissions, while CT showed a +$55K single high-cost ungroupable case.
GA Critical Access added about +$26K on 2 admissions with paid per admit up about $13.0K.

patterns_data.top_pattern: Rare high-cost IP Med/Surg outliers are creating one-off spikes across CA / PA / VA / KY
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: Rare IP Med/Surg admissions with very high paid per admit across CA / PA / VA / KY
key_driver_codes: DVTRCLI LG INT W/PERF ABSC NO BLEED
Revision of Hip or Knee Replacement with CC
Septicemia or Severe Sepsis without Mechanical Ventilation >96 Hours with MCC
patterns_data.pattern_details: A meaningful share of inpatient growth is coming from isolated, very expensive Med/Surg admissions rather than recurring utilization waves. The pattern spans CA and PA most visibly, with smaller related spikes in VA and KY across sepsis, chest procedures, revision joint cases, bowel surgery, cardiac procedures, and spinal cord cases. These are case-level outliers and should not be managed with broad policy changes until the individual cases are reviewed.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: One-off catastrophic or near-catastrophic admissions can materially move spend and require a different response than routine utilization growth.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Send the identified admissions for case-level medical necessity, coding, and stop-loss review before changing broader inpatient policy or provider strategy.
evidence_summary: CA spinal cord-related outliers added about +$0.2M, including single admissions of about +$104.0K and +$53.2K.
PA rare outliers included about +$94.6K for cardiac valve and catheterization with NSTEMI and about +$39.9K for bowel surgery.
Additional one-case spikes appeared in sepsis O.R. procedures, major chest procedures, revision hip or knee cases, and sepsis admissions across CA / KY / PA / VA.

patterns_data.top_pattern: Authorized acute hospital admissions are rising in VA and other emerging states
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: PPO Local Acute Hospital utilization in VA / OH / GA / NY
key_driver_codes: CARILION NEW RIVER VALLEY MEDICAL CENTER
patterns_data.pattern_details: This pattern is primarily about more authorized acute hospital use rather than pure price inflation. VA is the largest volume story, with additional emerging admission growth in OH and smaller clusters in GA / NY. Because unit cost is mixed, the first lever is admission management and provider-level utilization review.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: When admissions are the main driver, tighter front-end UM can slow spend faster than reimbursement changes alone.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Tighten admission management for authorized PPO Local acute hospital cases in VA / OH / GA / NY and audit repeat admitting providers for avoidable inpatient use.
evidence_summary: VA acute hospital spend rose about +$0.6M, driven by roughly 30 more admissions and 32 more claims.
OH added about +$0.3M with about 21 more admissions across Lehigh Valley, Lee Memorial, and cellulitis-related cases.
GA / NY added about +$80K, led by GA cellulitis admissions, while paid per admit was not consistently higher across the cluster.

patterns_data.top_pattern: Authorized claims in a Not Mapped facility bucket need a classification fix before site-of-care action
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: Facility type assignment for authorized PPO Local claims in VA / GA / OH / PA
key_driver_codes: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC

impact_summary.unit_cost_signal: not reliable until mapping is fixed

patterns_data.pattern_details: A separate validation issue is sitting in the facility classification itself: authorized claims are being grouped into a Not Mapped bucket, especially in VA and smaller clusters in GA, OH, and PA. That means site-of-care comparisons may be overstated or misdirected because some spend is not landing in a valid facility category. Correct classification should happen before any SNF, rehab, or hospital steering action.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Bad facility classification can create false site-of-care trends and send UM or network teams after the wrong setting.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Map Not Mapped authorized claims to valid facility types, fix the feed logic that is producing the bucket, and then rerun site-of-care results before acting on providers or benefit design.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The source groups carry unmapped facility values, so facility classification must be corrected before interpreting site-of-care or provider mix results.
evidence_summary: VA Not Mapped claims added about +$0.3M with 21 more admissions and 25 more claims.
GA Not Mapped added about +$92K, led by Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC (+$63K) and Ungroupable claims (+$29K).
OH / PA Not Mapped added about +$83K and was concentrated at Lee Memorial Hospital.

patterns_data.top_pattern: KY / VA inpatient oncology and specialty admissions are emerging at a small number of providers
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: KY / VA IP Med/Surg oncology and complex specialty admissions
key_driver_codes: Chemotherapy without Acute Leukemia as Secondary Diagnosis with MCC
Chemotherapy with Acute Leukemia as Secondary Diagnosis or with High Dose Chemotherapy Agent with MCC
patterns_data.pattern_details: A distinct inpatient oncology and specialty case pattern is emerging in KY / VA, led by University of Kentucky Albert B. Chandler Hospital and supported by smaller high-cost specialty admissions at Carilion. The biggest driver is inpatient chemotherapy, with additional complex cancer and specialty surgical cases. This should be managed separately from general Med/Surg outliers because site-of-care, clinical pathways, and reimbursement options are different.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Inpatient oncology episodes often have different UM, site-of-care, and contracting levers than routine inpatient admissions.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Route this cluster to oncology UM and reimbursement teams to assess inpatient chemo appropriateness, case-rate exposure, and outpatient alternatives where clinically appropriate.
evidence_summary: University of Kentucky Albert B. Chandler Hospital added about +$100.8K from chemotherapy without acute leukemia on 5 admissions at about $20.2K per admit.
A single high-dose or leukemia-related chemotherapy admission added about +$36.1K, and a head-and-neck cancer surgery case added about +$32.1K.
Carilion New River Valley Medical Center added about +$30.0K from a single complex respiratory O.R. admission.
